title: introduce-soft-timeout-probes-and-jittered-deadline-steering-to-reduce-batcher-stalls
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds softer timeout probing and randomized deadline steering to reduce batcher queue stalls and KV-pin starvation; no user-visible API changes.
commit_list: a1d3f7c: implement jittered deadline steering and soft-probe admission hooks
b2e8c92: KV pin awareness in scheduler + probe lease bookkeeping
c3f12ab: add integration tests and metrics for probe/backoff behavior
body:
Context and motivation: We observed periodic micro-stalls in the continuous batching scheduler under mixed KV-heavy and short-lived inference workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to: (1) tight deterministic deadline windows causing synchronized probe storms when many requests reach the same soft timeout boundary, and (2) KV-pinned requests monopolizing head-of-queue positions leading to starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces two cooperative mechanisms: (A) soft-timeout probes with randomized jitter and exponential backoff to avoid synchronized probe storms, and (B) deadline-steering that biases scheduling decisions away from long-KV pins during probe windows so short requests have a better chance to complete. Both are runtime-only scheduler changes with no public API surface.

Summary of changes: - New probe subsystem (internal/serving/batcher/probe.go) implements soft probes: instead of hard preemption at N ms, a soft probe flags requests for lightweight admission checks. Probes are jittered +/- up to 25% and use an adaptive backoff per origin to reduce re-probing frequency for offenders. - Scheduler modifications (internal/serving/batcher/scheduler.go): when a soft-probed request is present, scheduler evaluates a deadline-steering score that temporarily reduces priority of requests with active KV pins and high predicted token cost. The steering is proportional to probe urgency and decays over a configurable grace window. - KV awareness (internal/serving/kv/cache_manager.go): probes annotate requests with kv_pin_estimate and attach a short-lived lease so the scheduler can reason about potential blocking. - Observability (pkg/observe/metrics/batcher_metrics.go): new metrics added: batcher_probe_count, probe_backoff_rate, deadline_steer_evictions, kv_pin_lease_count; histograms for probe-to-exec latency. - Tests and documentation: deterministic integration tests (tests/integration/batcher_stall_test.go) that simulate mixed workloads and assert tail-latency and throughput; runbook guidance for tuning the new knobs (docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md).

Design rationale: - Soft probes instead of hard timeouts: allow scheduler to make better packing decisions rather than preempting work. - Jitter reduces global synchronization under load spikes. - Steering uses lightweight heuristics (kv_pin_estimate + token_cost) to avoid complex global optimization loops; we prefer predictable, auditable behavior. - Backoff state is kept per-origin and capped to avoid state explosion.

Performance summary (internal CI/bench): - Baseline: mixed workload (60% KV-pin heavy long requests, 40% short chat-like requests) tail P95 token latency = 420ms over 30m window. - After change (default knobs): P95 = 320ms (-23%), P99 = 640ms (-14%), median unchanged. - CPU/GPU utilization: slight increase in scheduler CPU (~3%) but overall token throughput steady. - Under synthetic probe storms, observed probe storms reduced by ~78% due to jitter+backoff.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation + unit tests - [x] Integration test reproducing previous stall - [x] Metrics + dashboards updated - [x] Runbook draft - [x] Benchmarks and resource budget sanity - [x] Security review (no user data exfiltration risk)

Files changed (high level): - internal/serving/batcher/scheduler.go: add steering score, hook into admission path, unit tests for decay logic - internal/serving/batcher/probe.go: new file implementing probe lifecycle, jitter/backoff policy, probe metrics - internal/serving/kv/cache_manager.go: expose kv_pin_estimate and short leases for scheduler; small refactor to avoid locking hotspots - pkg/observe/metrics/batcher_metrics.go: new metrics and tags - tests/integration/batcher_stall_test.go: synthetic workload harness, asserts on tail-latency and fairness - docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md: knobs explanation and suggested defaults

Review conversation (excerpt): - Marco Liu (review): "Nice isolation of probe lifecycle. One concern: the per-origin backoff map could grow unbounded in high-tenant systems. Can we auto-evict or TTL entries?" - Author (Aisha): "Good catch — added TTL+LRU cap (configurable) and a cleanup tick; updated tests to validate eviction behavior." - Riley Thompson (review): "Can we avoid any mem alloc on the hot path for the steering score?" - Author: "We changed steering to use a preallocated scoring buffer and removed allocations in hot path; benchmark shows <1% extra allocs." - Priya Desai (approver): "Verified metrics and runbook; approved after a small nit on doc wording." - Additional comments: one infra CI failure (flake in tests/integration/flake_x) was rerun and passed.

CI and stability notes: - CI run: unit (pass), integration (pass after one rerun), benchmark jobs (internal perf cluster) completed and attached. - Notable flaky test fixed in this branch: tests/integration/flake_x — flake existed due to timing assumptions; made test robust to small timing variance.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: - No API changes. - Feature gated behind runtime flag batcher.enable_soft_probes=false by default in main; rollout plan: enable for 10% rollout on Dedicated and Hosted canary pools for two weeks, monitor probe metrics + tail latency; then ramp to 50/100. - If regressions observed, automatic fallback policy in console will flip the flag and route to non-probed variant.

Operational guidance: - Default knobs are tuned for mixed production traffic; for KV-heavy enterprise workloads, increase kv_pin_lease_ms and reduce probe_jitter_pct. - Runbook (docs/runbooks/batcher-tuning.md) includes alert thresholds: probe_backoff_rate > 0.1 sustained and deadline_steer_evictions > 5/min should trigger investigation.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main on 2025-12-02 after approvals. Merge commit: "squash: introduce soft probes + deadline steering (ENG-4012)".
